The accompanying act - the Proposal for the Law on Budget Execution - is also on the agenda. Last week, the House of Peoples failed to give majority support to the budget proposal, not due to the Government's proposal, but because of the submitted amendments, which, as explained, would necessitate a challenging redistribution of funds from one item to another 'heavy' one worth over 20 million KM. The leadership of the House of Representatives demands that the budget be confirmed in both houses by the New Year, which is crucial for it to come into effect and for the Federation of BiH, after a prolonged period, to enter the next fiscal year with a timely adopted budget. Emphasizing that there will be sufficient time before the New Year for the House of Peoples to reconvene and approve the budget in the same text after the session of the House of Representatives, as the agreed act is essential for it to take effect on time. This was also unequivocally announced by the Alliance for a Better Future of BiH, while the Social Democratic Party conditioned their support on the approval of their party's submitted amendments. The Democratic Front has firmly stated their opposition to the budget, arguing that it lacks any key development components. The Government, as proposer, unveiled a notable total budget figure of 2,598,862,123 KM, marking a 65 million increase from the draft act.
